issues.summary: (MEDIUM) The bug-063 proxy status guard only rejected >= 400: the client is built without follow_redirects, so a reverse proxy's 301/302/307/308 (http->https or /mcp trailing-slash canonicalization) surfaced with an HTML body, bypassed the guard, and was written verbatim to stdout — the same JSON-RPC stream desync bug-063 targeted, from the redirect range (multi-line body desyncs the reader session-wide; an empty body hangs the request).
issues.fix_note: Guard now rejects everything outside 2xx (only a 2xx can carry a JSON-RPC/SSE payload), surfacing an id-keyed JSON-RPC error and keeping the loop alive. No behavioural proxy suite exists (bug-051/063 precedent) — the fix marker pins the guard.

issues.summary: (LOW) bug-072 residuals: check_embedding_dimension probed embed(['test']) INSIDE maybe_write_lock(fix) on every fix run; _reembed_null_rows fell back to LIVE embeds under the lock on any cache miss; and rows NULLed DURING the locked run (dimension-mismatch NULLing, annotation/mention/oversize rewrites) were absent from prefetch by construction — up to 500+500 sequential HTTP round-trips while holding the shared write lock, the exact cross-writer stall bug-072 was created to remove.
issues.fix_note: Three-part fix: (1) the dimension probe runs in the unlocked prefetch phase (probe_embedding_dim -> embedding_cache['expected_dim']); (2) the locked re-embed never live-embeds when a cache dict is present (cache misses stay NULL); (3) do_check_health runs a second UNLOCKED prefetch pass after the fix run and applies it under a short lock with content revalidated in the UPDATE (bug-077 guard) — single-run convergence without HTTP under the lock. Class gate: test_structural_gates.py::test_check_health_never_embeds_under_write_lock.

issues.summary: (LOW) bug-040/041 residual: the fix excluded episode rows from recall_counts' CONSTRUCTION but both LOOKUP sites still keyed by raw row id — episode #N co-recalled with memory #N inherited the memory's (recall_count, last_recalled_at), inflating the episode's confidence score (ranking + reported value). Gated behind CONFIDENCE_ENABLED (default off), so default deployments were unaffected.
issues.fix_note: Both lookup sites (ranking loop in _apply_recall_scoring and the response confidence loop) now short-circuit episodes to (0, '') — closing the lookup side of the invariant the bug-041 docstring states ('an episode id must never key into a memories query'). Regression: test_audit_r3.py::test_episode_confidence_ignores_colliding_memory_recall_count.

issues.summary: (HIGH) Vector scan window was derived from the response limit: _search_vector fetched only the newest min(MAX_MEMORIES, max(limit*10, 100)) rows before cosine ranking, so a default limit=10 recall ranked only the newest 100 rows and anything older was structurally invisible to the vector retriever. The 2.4.38 limit clamp (bug-032) then closed the only escape hatch (callers passing a huge limit), collapsing LMEB LongMemEval from ~78 to 38.68 on MiniLM; re-running the harness with the clamp bypassed restored 76.99, confirming the window as the sole cause. The MAX_MEMORIES=500 default additionally capped reach below real corpus sizes even for unclamped callers.
issues.fix_note: Scan breadth decoupled from response size: _search_vector now fetches and ranks the newest MAX_MEMORIES rows regardless of the caller's limit, and the MAX_MEMORIES default is raised 500 -> 10000 (CPERSONA_MAX_MEMORIES env for larger corpora, e.g. benchmarks). The bug-032 response clamp is unchanged and correct. The LIKE fallback needs no change: its LIMIT applies after the content predicate, capping matched rows rather than scanned rows, so old rows were always reachable there. test_scan_window.py pins both contracts (window decoupling, 10000 default, LIKE reachability).

issues.summary: (MEDIUM) Dirty reads on the shared connection: connection() yielded the writer's own aiosqlite connection, and WAL snapshot isolation only exists ACROSS connections — a SELECT executed inside another coroutine's open transaction observed its uncommitted rows. do_store's dedup probe could match an import row that was later rolled back (the acknowledged store then existed nowhere: silent loss), and recall/get_contents could serve phantom rows. Found by the 2.5.0b1 hybrid audit (Anthropic concurrency finder), mechanism self-verified.
issues.fix_note: Read seam moved to a dedicated read connection (_get_read_db), re-keyed on the current write connection after a reboot, with any implicit transaction rolled back on scope exit (FTS5's integrity-check is spelled as an INSERT and would otherwise pin the WAL snapshot forever). Regression: test_audit_2500b1.py::test_read_seam_does_not_see_uncommitted_writes / _unpins_snapshot_on_scope_exit / _rekeys_after_reboot.

issues.summary: (LOW, latent) get_db() memoised the connection before schema/migrations completed: a failed boot left _db set, so every later caller took the fast path and received a half-initialised connection; concurrent first-touch callers could also run the committing migration ladder twice. Unreachable in the production boot order (init_db is awaited before the transport starts).
issues.fix_note: The global is published only after _init_schema succeeds, under _init_lock; a failed boot closes the connection and leaves _db unset so the retry re-runs the idempotent ladder. Regression: test_audit_2500b1.py::test_get_db_is_not_memoized_on_failed_init.

issues.summary: (MEDIUM) merge_memories(mode='move') ran the copy and the source wipe as two separate locked transactions. Any writer queued behind the merge on the FIFO write lock could insert into the source between the merge commit and the delete — do_delete_agent_data then wiped an acknowledged row that was never copied (deterministic loss, not just a crash window). A crash between the transactions degraded the move to a copy, and a no-persist pause landing in between silently skipped the wipe under ok:true.
issues.fix_note: The wipe runs INSIDE the merge transaction via the _delete_agent_rows leaf; only the non-DB side effects (calibration purge, remote namespace purge) run post-commit. Regression: test_audit_2500b1.py::test_merge_move_is_one_atomic_unit / _deletes_source_in_same_call.

issues.summary: (LOW, vestigial surface) The queue drain committed do_archive_episode's INSERT and _delete_task's DELETE as two transactions: a crash (or a failure of the delete alone) replayed the bare, non-idempotent INSERT on the next drain and duplicated the episode. No production path enqueues today (bug-006 removed the last one), so only crash-recovered legacy rows hit this.
issues.fix_note: do_archive_episode is split into _prepare_episode_row (validation + embedding HTTP, outside the lock) and the _insert_episode_row leaf; the drain runs the episode INSERT and the task-row DELETE in ONE transaction. Regression: test_audit_2500b1.py::test_drain_archive_is_single_transaction / _archives_and_deletes_task_atomically; FIFO dispatch re-pinned in test_task_queue.py::test_fifo_ordering.

issues.summary: (LOW) The drain distinguished only raise-vs-return: a handler-returned {ok:false} dict (e.g. a crash-recovered legacy archive task with no summary) was deleted and logged 'completed' — silently discarding exactly the rows the crash-recovery queue exists to preserve.
issues.fix_note: A failure-shaped return routes into the retry/discard path like a raise, so legacy summary-less rows fail visibly (error log + max-retries discard) instead of masquerading as successes. Regression: test_audit_2500b1.py::test_drain_treats_failure_dict_as_failure.

issues.summary: (MEDIUM) do_export_memories opened the destination with open(path, 'w'), destroying the previous backup the moment the export started; a mid-export fault (disk full, kill) left a truncated JSONL that do_import_memories restored 'successfully' (silent partial restore of the disaster-recovery tool). The pre-write COUNT queries could also disagree with the later row SELECTs (torn header). Found by the 2.5.0b1 hybrid audit (Anthropic fault finder).
issues.fix_note: Export writes to a temp file and os.replace()s on success; the header is derived from the fetched rows so it always matches the body; import validates the body against the header and rejects truncated files with a full rollback. Regression: test_audit_2500b1.py::test_export_failure_preserves_previous_backup / test_import_rejects_truncated_file.

issues.summary: (LOW) Export omitted recall_count / last_recalled_at entirely and import re-stamped created_at with import time: a backup round-trip zeroed the recall-frequency scoring boost (utils.py raw_boost) and reordered the vector scan window / episode session probes that ORDER BY created_at.
issues.fix_note: All three columns ride the export record and the import INSERT (created_at via COALESCE for older files). Merge's SELECT/INSERT carries them via the same audit batch. Regression: test_audit_2500b1.py::test_roundtrip_preserves_recall_stats_and_created_at.

issues.summary: (LOW) do_delete_agent_data left the agent's pending_memory_tasks rows in place: a crash-recovered task for the wiped agent would re-INSERT episode/profile rows, silently resurrecting data for a deleted agent.
issues.fix_note: _delete_agent_rows clears pending_memory_tasks in the same transaction as the other tables and reports deleted_pending_tasks. Regression: test_audit_2500b1.py::test_delete_agent_data_purges_pending_tasks.

issues.summary: (LOW) Episode keywords were bound to db.execute untouched: a JSON-array value (the natural hand-authored format) reached sqlite3 as a Python list -> InterfaceError -> the whole import aborted, while the same file previewed cleanly under dry_run because the binding lived on the write path only (type-validation parity gap, distinct from the count-parity class bug-056/070/071).
issues.fix_note: Field extraction/coercion happens on BOTH paths before the dry_run branch; arrays are joined to the documented space-separated string. Regression: test_audit_2500b1.py::test_import_keywords_array_is_coerced.

issues.summary: (LOW) _save_calibration_state wrote the sidecar in place (open 'w' + json.dump) and swallowed OSError with a log line: a mid-write kill corrupted the sidecar for EVERY agent (loader returns None; with auto-calibration off, all agents silently fall back to the global default threshold), and do_calibrate_threshold returned ok:true even when persistence failed.
issues.fix_note: Sidecar written via temp + os.replace; the save returns success and calibrate_threshold surfaces it as sidecar_persisted. Regression: test_audit_2500b1.py::test_sidecar_save_failure_returns_false.

issues.summary: (LOW) do_set_recall_precision applied the in-memory beta override before calling do_calibrate_threshold and rolled it back only on an ok:false RETURN — a RAISED calibration failure (transient DB lock, numpy fault) leaked the un-persisted beta into process memory, and the next routine calibration persisted a gate at a beta the caller was told failed to apply.
issues.fix_note: The calibrate call is wrapped so a raise takes the same rollback path as ok:false. Regression: test_audit_2500b1.py::test_set_recall_precision_rolls_back_beta_on_raise.

issues.summary: (LOW) duplicate_content ran before oversized_content in HEALTH_CHECKS: the oversized fixer truncates content to MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH and can mint fresh duplicate groups after the dup check already passed. The bug-059 residual re-run reported them (not silent), but a single fix pass could not converge.
issues.fix_note: oversized_content (and the other content rewriters, which already preceded) run before duplicate_content. Regression: test_audit_2500b1.py::test_health_checks_order_oversized_before_duplicate.

issues.summary: (HIGH) Five fixers mutated rows WITHOUT the locked = 0 guard: check_invalid_json (source/metadata -> '{}'), check_invalid_timestamp (timestamp -> created_at), check_timestamp_format_drift (timestamp normalisation), check_invalid_source_type (source -> anonymous default) and deep_anonymous_source (source rewrite) — check_health(fix=true) could rewrite a locked memory's source/metadata/timestamp, violating lock_memory's 'never lost or altered by maintenance' contract. Content-destructive fixers were already guarded, which is why earlier audits reported the guard as present. Found by the 2.5.0b1 hybrid audit (Gemini lifecycle finder), self-verified.
issues.fix_note: All five fixers carry locked = 0 (the id-keyed ones guard by id AND locked = 0). Locked rows with invalid fields now surface as residual issues instead of being silently rewritten. Regression: test_audit_2500b1.py::test_fixers_do_not_mutate_locked_rows.

issues.summary: (LOW) do_lock_memory / do_unlock_memory ignored the UPDATE rowcount: a row deleted between the ownership pre-check and the UPDATE (they straddle an await) was acknowledged as locked/unlocked — a user's 'lock this rule so it can never be lost' returned ok while protecting nothing. Sibling mutations (delete/update) already checked rowcount (bug-024).
issues.fix_note: rowcount == 0 returns a not-found error. Regression: test_audit_2500b1.py::test_lock_memory_vanished_row_is_an_error.

issues.summary: (LOW, defense-in-depth) The remote-mode by-id rehydrate fetch dropped the agent_id predicate (isolation_where without agent) — ownership rested entirely on the remote index's namespace matching DB ownership; a desynced or mis-seeded index would have surfaced another agent's row with no agent-side backstop. No in-tree path plants a foreign id (AUTOINCREMENT + owner-namespace writers), hence LOW. Cross-confirmed by both audit providers.
issues.fix_note: iso_fetch / iso_ep_fetch carry agent_id — the fetch fails closed.

issues.summary: (LOW) _calibrate_fused_gate skipped any result whose integer id equalled the pseudo-query id without checking the memory/episode namespace — an episode sharing the memory's AUTOINCREMENT id was silently dropped from the calibration curve (residual of the fixed bug-040/041/084 collision class). Impact: one omitted sample per colliding query; distributions hold hundreds of points.
issues.fix_note: The skip applies only when the row is the pseudo-query MEMORY (_is_episode_result discriminates).

issues.summary: (LOW) do_import_memories iterated the input file with blocking I/O inside transaction(): a slow disk/network mount stalled the event loop — and with it every reader and writer — for as long as the read took, while the write lock was held (same shape as the fixed bug-072 network-under-lock class, disk edition).
issues.fix_note: The file is read fully before entering the write seam; the transaction loops over in-memory lines.

issues.summary: (LOW, cosmetic) status() evaluated _now() twice (once in _decay, once for the remaining-TTL subtraction): crossing the TTL boundary between the two produced the contradictory {paused: true, ttl_remaining_seconds: 0}. Write guards call is_paused() themselves, so no write was ever mis-gated. Vendored module — upstream sync tracked separately.
issues.fix_note: The clock is snapshotted once and passed through _decay(now).

issues.summary: (LOW) make_skipped_response rewrote only the literal 'id' key: write tools returning action-specific keys (deleted_id/updated_id/locked_id/unlocked_id) echoed the caller-supplied id under ok:true, so a consumer branching on the id field (instead of the authoritative persisted:false) inferred success during a no-persist pause. Vendored module — upstream sync tracked separately.
issues.fix_note: The action-specific *_id keys are nulled in the skipped response. Regression: test_audit_2500b1.py::test_no_persist_skip_nulls_action_id_keys.

issues.summary: (LOW) checkup.py (the read-only cron CLI) triggered get_db()'s full boot path: a report-only run silently migrated a version-stale DB from a monitoring cron, and crashed outright on a read-only file/filesystem before any check ran ('read-only' in its docstring meant no --fix repairs, not no writes at all).
issues.fix_note: checkup without --fix sets database.SKIP_BOOT_MIGRATIONS: session pragma only, no schema/FTS/ladder writes; a stale schema surfaces through check_schema_version instead. Regression: test_audit_2500b1.py::test_skip_boot_migrations_writes_nothing.

issues.summary: (MEDIUM, semantic change approved 2026-07-15) do_store's dedup probes exact-matched the project/channel bucket while reads use γ semantics: a bucket write ('X') did not see an identical global-pool row, inserted a duplicate, and recall('X') — which surfaces X ∪ '' — returned both copies. Write-side dedup and read-side visibility disagreed.
issues.fix_note: The probes check the γ-VISIBLE scope: bucket writes collide with the global pool (both axes), global writes probe the global pool only, sibling buckets stay distinct (bug-044 precedent). Import/merge keep exact-bucket probes deliberately (restore/merge fidelity); the v12 UNIQUE indexes stay exact-bucket as the TOCTOU backstop. Regression: test_audit_2500b1.py::test_store_dedup_is_gamma_visible / _gamma_channel_axis.

issues.summary: (LOW, semantic change approved 2026-07-15) The confidence temporal span was MIN/MAX(timestamp) over the WHOLE agent: a recall scoped to one project/channel had its confidence curve scaled by timestamps from unrelated buckets (an ancient row in another project stretched time_range_hours for everyone).
issues.fix_note: _apply_recall_scoring computes the span over the recall's own isolation axes; corpus-wide callers (gate calibration) keep the agent-wide default. Regression: test_audit_2500b1.py::test_temporal_span_is_scoped_to_recall_axes.

issues.summary: (LOW, latent) _get_read_db held the shared _init_lock while re-calling get_db(), which re-acquires the same lock when _db is unset — a close_db racing a read-seam first-touch self-deadlocked the coroutine (asyncio.Lock is not reentrant). Found by the post-fix regression hunt (Gemini) on the 2.5.0b1 delta, verified and fixed before merge.
issues.fix_note: The read seam owns a dedicated _read_lock; ordering is always _read_lock -> _init_lock, never the reverse. Regression: test_audit_2500b1.py::test_read_seam_survives_closed_db_race.

issues.summary: (LOW) The drain's unlocked prepare window (embedding HTTP) raced delete_agent_data / merge move: the wipe purges the agent's queue rows (bug-093), but a task fetched BEFORE the wipe still inserted its episode afterwards — resurrecting data for a deleted agent, with the task-row DELETE silently matching 0 rows. Narrower residue of the pre-b1 behaviour (where queue rows survived wipes entirely); closed before merge.
issues.fix_note: The task-row DELETE runs first inside the drain transaction and doubles as the claim token: rowcount 0 (row vanished during prepare = agent wiped) vetoes the episode INSERT. Regression: test_audit_2500b1.py::test_drain_does_not_resurrect_wiped_agent.

issues.summary: (MEDIUM) The bug-091 truncation guard validated memory/episode counts only: a backup cut exactly at the episode/profile boundary passed validation and restored a profile-less corpus with ok:true — the same silent-partial-restore class bug-091 closed. The abort response also dropped the per-line `errors` diagnostics and claimed 'rolled back' on the write-free dry_run path. Found by the post-fix regression hunt (Anthropic) on the 2.5.0b1 delta.
issues.fix_note: The export header carries profile_count and the import validates all three counts; abort responses keep `errors` and say 'aborted (dry run — nothing was written)' on previews. Export/sidecar temp files are PID-suffixed against cross-process collisions (bug-091 hardening). Regression: test_audit_2500b1.py::test_import_rejects_file_cut_at_profile_boundary.

issues.summary: (LOW) do_delete_agent_data's no-persist skipped response kept the pre-bug-093 three-count shape while the real response gained deleted_pending_tasks — the schema differed across pause state. Found by the post-fix regression hunt (Anthropic); the final fix-verification pass caught the same drift in do_merge_memories' skeleton (missing source/target/strategy/mode echo keys), fixed together.
issues.fix_note: Both skipped skeletons mirror their real response shapes: delete_agent_data carries deleted_pending_tasks: 0 and merge_memories echoes source_agent_id/target_agent_id/strategy/mode. Regression: test_audit_2500b1.py::test_no_persist_delete_shape_matches_real_response (covers both).

issues.summary: (LOW) SKIP_BOOT_MIGRATIONS (bug-105) promised a write-free report-only boot, but get_db() still ran makedirs + connect: a checkup pointed at a mistyped path created a 0-byte schema-less DB file and the checks then failed noisily against it. Found by the post-fix regression hunt (Anthropic).
issues.fix_note: Report-only boots raise FileNotFoundError for a missing DB path instead of creating anything. Regression: test_audit_2500b1.py::test_skip_boot_migrations_refuses_missing_db.

issues.summary: (LOW, pre-existing — present in 2.5.0a2 and earlier) check_oversized_content's truncation UPDATE could land exactly on an existing same-bucket row's content, violating idx_memories_dedup_content: the IntegrityError surfaced as check_crashed on EVERY subsequent fix run, leaving the row permanently unfixable (breaks the bug-097 single-pass-convergence promise). Found by the post-fix regression hunt (Anthropic) while auditing the check reordering.
issues.fix_note: On an IntegrityError the oversized row is deleted as a duplicate of the colliding survivor (keep-existing, never-touch-locked — the dup fixer's policy). Regression: test_audit_2500b1.py::test_oversized_truncation_collision_converges. bug-127 generalized this guard to check_memory_annotation/check_discord_mention via a shared helper.

issues.summary: (HIGH) 2.5.0b1 audit C07 (subsumes C11): _parse_timestamp_utc ran astimezone() on naive datetimes, assuming system-local time. last_recalled_at and episodes.created_at are written naive via SQLite datetime('now') (which emits UTC), so on any non-UTC host recall-boost decay and the episode-boundary factor were silently shifted by the local UTC offset (repro-confirmed: JST +9h). Cross-provider audit pipeline (agy finders + Sonnet verify + Fable adjudication).
issues.fix_note: Naive timestamps are anchored as UTC by invariant in _parse_timestamp_utc and _format_memory_timestamp before any conversion. Prevention: ruff DTZ (flake8-datetimez) enabled in [tool.ruff.lint] bans new naive datetime construction statically. Regression: test_audit_2500b2.py::test_parse_timestamp_naive_is_utc.

issues.summary: (HIGH) 2.5.0b1 audit C10: the episode-boundary penalty multiplied _cosine/_rrf_score/_rsf_score in place, but the only re-sort lived inside the CONFIDENCE_ENABLED block (default off). Under default config (rrf + confidence off + penalty on) the penalty never re-ordered output or downstream truncation — a ranking no-op.
issues.fix_note: _apply_recall_scoring re-sorts homogeneous fusion-ordered lists after applying the penalty when confidence is off; cascade stage order is intentionally preserved (bug-018 doctrine). Regression: test_audit_2500b2.py::test_episode_penalty_resorts_fusion_results. bug-126 re-opened and closed the profile-row hole in the same re-sort.

issues.summary: (MEDIUM) 2.5.0b1 audit C25 (bug-114 root family): deep_orphaned_episodes compared mixed-format timestamp strings lexicographically — memories.timestamp is offset-aware ISO-8601 with a 'T' separator while episode windows may be naive datetime('now') format with a space, and 'T' > ' ' makes the range test garbage, yielding false-positive orphans.
issues.fix_note: The range test normalises both sides through SQLite datetime(), which converts offset-aware values to UTC and passes naive (already-UTC) values through. Regression: test_audit_2500b2.py::test_orphan_check_survives_mixed_timestamp_formats.

issues.summary: (LOW) 2.5.0b1 audit C20: _apply_preview truncated injected rows that carry no ref handle ([Profile] injections, external_context echoes), leaving no get_contents path to the full text — the content became permanently unreachable through the MCP surface.
issues.fix_note: Preview truncation now skips rows without a ref; only expandable rows are trimmed. Regression: test_audit_2500b2.py::test_preview_skips_refless_rows.

issues.summary: (MEDIUM) 2.5.0b1 audit C36: version-gated FTS migrations (v11 contamination rebuild, v13 trigger narrowing) were permanently skipped when the schema version advanced while FTS_ENABLED=false — the stamp recorded them as done, and FTS_SQL's CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS kept the stale trigger bodies on re-enable.
issues.fix_note: get_db() probes the memories_fts_au DDL itself (column-scoped 'AFTER UPDATE OF content'); a stale or missing body drops the update triggers for recreation and arms the durable backfill bit so the rebuild clears stale trigrams. Regression: test_audit_2500b2.py::test_stale_fts_trigger_modernised_on_boot.

issues.summary: (LOW) 2.5.0b1 audit C45 (bug-111 sibling class): the no-persist skeletons for calibrate_threshold and set_recall_precision diverged from the real success payloads — calibrate carried a phantom sample_size key and none of the real keys; set_recall_precision dropped cleared/fused_gate/calibrate and nulled the resolved echo values. (check_health/deep_check adjudicated by-design: they run the real diagnostic with fix downgraded, which is a superior contract.)
issues.fix_note: Both guards moved after pure param validation (invalid input returns the real error even while paused, the import/merge doctrine) and both skeletons mirror the real success shape. Regression: test_audit_2500b2.py::test_calibrate_skeleton_mirrors_real_shape.

issues.summary: (HIGH) 2.5.0b1 audit C03+C04: Gate 2's isolation check accepted any statement whose post-WHERE text merely contained the substring AGENT_ID ('OR agent_id IS NULL', a comment, an unrelated column), and interpolated DML targets (f"DELETE FROM {table}") collapsed to a placeholder and were skipped entirely — unscoped DML could be certified isolation-safe.
issues.fix_note: The gate strips SQL comments, requires a real agent_id conjunct (comparison predicate, no paren-depth-0 OR), treats interpolated DML targets as agent-scoped pseudo-targets, accepts the iso-parameter conduit, and exempts FTS5 self-referencing control commands. Teeth: test_audit_2500b2.py::test_gate_rejects_or_weakened_predicate.

issues.summary: (LOW) 2.5.0b1 audit C29: _content_excluded returned True for an empty content string whenever any exclude filter was set (''.startswith-in-reverse matches everything), silently dropping legitimately-empty-content memories from recall.
issues.fix_note: Empty/whitespace-only content never matches an exclude filter. Regression: test_audit_2500b2.py::test_content_excluded_empty_content_not_dropped.

issues.summary: (MEDIUM) 2.5.0b1 audit C02: CI ran ruff+pytest but never invoked verify-issues.sh, so the 113-entry regression registry (file-pinned fix markers) was not enforced as a merge gate — a refactor could silently strip a fix marker.
issues.fix_note: Dedicated verify-issues CI job runs scripts/verify-issues.sh on every PR/master push.

issues.summary: (MEDIUM) bug-118 follow-up: the boot rebuild's execution condition omitted fts_triggers_stale, so a stale-trigger boot armed the durable backfill bit and modernised the trigger DDL but deferred the actual FTS rebuild to the NEXT boot - the pending bit (and any stale trigrams) survived the whole current process lifetime.
issues.fix_note: Rebuild condition now includes fts_triggers_stale, so the recovery rebuilds in the same boot that detected the stale trigger.

issues.summary: (HIGH) test_stale_fts_trigger_modernised_on_boot re-pointed database._db with a bare '= None', orphaning the session-shared aiosqlite connection; its NON-daemon worker thread blocked interpreter exit after the suite summary, so every CI test job hung to the 6-hour limit (2.5.0b2 was merged while those jobs were still running).
issues.fix_note: Reboot-pattern tests go through database.close_db() (which closes write+read connections); close_db's docstring carries the doctrine, and the CI test job now has timeout-minutes:15 so any future hang fails fast instead of masking as a 6h cancel. Class prevention (post-b3): tests/test_structural_gates.py::test_no_orphaning_connection_repoint statically rejects any database._db/_read_db re-point with no prior close()/stash in scope (inline `# orphan-waiver:` escape; teeth test included).

issues.summary: Empty-query recall routed through cascade recency rows with no relevance score, so the unscored volume rule silently rejected every result when the agent had fewer than 100 memories.
issues.fix_note: The quality gate now bypasses the unscored volume rule only for pure-recency empty-query recall. Regression: test_audit_2500b3.py::test_empty_query_recall_bypasses_unscored_volume_gate.

issues.summary: A profile injection row carried no fusion score, so the all-rows homogeneity guard skipped the episode-boundary re-sort and silently defeated the bug-115 penalty under default config.
issues.fix_note: The episode-penalty re-sort now checks fusion-score homogeneity across scored rows only and sinks profile sentinels with a negative-infinity sort key. Regression: test_audit_2500b3.py::test_episode_penalty_resorts_with_profile_row.

issues.summary: Annotation and Discord-mention content rewrites used bare UPDATEs, so a dedup-index collision crashed the health fix loop and left the colliding row permanently dirty.
issues.fix_note: All content-rewriting checks now share an IntegrityError guard that deletes the unlocked rewritten duplicate while preserving the existing survivor. Regression: test_audit_2500b3.py::test_memory_annotation_collision_deletes_rewritten_duplicate and test_audit_2500b3.py::test_discord_mention_collision_deletes_rewritten_duplicate.

issues.summary: Cross-channel duplicate repair kept MIN(id), which could delete the channel='' shared row and silently narrow recall visibility.
issues.fix_note: The survivor subquery now prefers a channel='' shared row and falls back to MIN(id) only when no shared copy exists. Regression: test_audit_2500b3.py::test_duplicate_content_prefers_shared_channel_survivor.

issues.summary: NULL-embedding prefetch made one timeout-bounded backend call per row without consulting or feeding the health circuit breaker.
issues.fix_note: Prefetch now skips an already faulted backend, embeds rows in chunks of 32, records chunk failures, and exits once the breaker latches. Regression: test_audit_2500b3.py::test_prefetch_null_embeddings_skips_faulted_backend and test_audit_2500b3.py::test_prefetch_null_embeddings_batches_rows. CORRECTION (bug-274): the "records chunk failures" half never fired. It sat in an `except` clause, and the embedding call reports transport failure by returning no embeddings rather than by raising, so the branch was dead on an unreachable endpoint. Neither named regression drove it — one asserts the backend is skipped when already faulted (the client is never called) and the other covers batching on the success path — and the only failing double raised, which the real client does not. Repaired in 2.5.9.

issues.summary: Import accepted unconstrained caller-supplied paths and read files of unbounded size into memory, allowing arbitrary server-readable data ingestion and denial of service.
issues.fix_note: Import now shares export path confinement, rejects files above MAX_IMPORT_BYTES before reading, and is annotated destructive. Regression: test_audit_2500b3.py::test_import_rejects_unconfined_and_oversized_paths.

issues.summary: Merge omitted created_at, recall_count, and last_recalled_at when copying memories, silently resetting the ranking history used by confidence and decay.
issues.fix_note: Merge now carries created_at, recall_count, and last_recalled_at from each source memory into the target row. Regression: test_audit_2500b3.py::test_merge_preserves_memory_ranking_metadata.

issues.summary: Import and merge inserted memories without upserting them into the remote vector index, making bulk-loaded rows invisible to remote vector recall.
issues.fix_note: Import and merge now batch-upsert each inserted memory to the target agent's remote namespace after the database transaction commits. Regression: test_audit_2500b3.py::test_import_syncs_inserted_memories_to_remote_index and test_audit_2500b3.py::test_merge_remote_sync_respects_vector_mode.

issues.summary: Bare int() and float() environment parsing made any malformed numeric setting raise during module import and crash the entire server.
issues.fix_note: Numeric environment settings now use warning-and-default coercion helpers so malformed values degrade independently without blocking import. Regression: tests/test_config_parsing.py::test_invalid_numeric_env_values_fall_back_to_defaults.

issues.summary: The HTTP Bearer authentication tests reimplemented the nested middleware's authorization decision, so a regression in the real middleware could pass CI.
issues.fix_note: BearerTokenMiddleware is now module-level and parameterized so tests exercise the real ASGI middleware. Regression: tests/test_v2435_bugfixes.py::test_auth_missing_or_blank_header_is_rejected.

issues.summary: The untested stdio proxy dropped valid SSE data lines without a space after the colon and emitted no JSON-RPC error when a malformed request's ID could not be recovered.
issues.fix_note: The proxy now accepts both SSE data-field forms and always emits errors with null for unrecoverable IDs. Regression: tests/test_proxy_stdio.py::test_sse_data_lines_allow_optional_space and test_write_error_always_emits_response.

issues.summary: Profile injection was copy-pasted across all three recall fusion strategies, so changing one copy could silently make profile behavior strategy-dependent.
issues.fix_note: Profile injection now has one _append_profile_rows helper called at the original position in cascade, RRF, and RSF recall. Regression: tests/test_audit_2500b3.py::test_profile_injection_shared_across_recall_strategies.

issues.summary: Row-level admin operations silently skipped ownership enforcement when the kernel-injected agent_id was omitted.
issues.fix_note: Optional-agent row operations now log a warning when they run unscoped while preserving the injected-trust behavior. Regression: tests/test_audit_2500b3.py::test_unscoped_delete_memory_warns_without_changing_behavior.

issues.summary: Boot silently accepted a persisted schema version newer than the build and then operated on a schema the older code may not understand.
issues.fix_note: Boot now warns when the persisted schema version is newer than SCHEMA_VERSION without refusing startup or changing the version stamp. Regression: tests/test_audit_2500b3.py::test_newer_schema_version_warns_without_blocking_boot.

issues.summary: check_invalid_source_type(fix=True) counted every offending row in `count` but the fix loop only saw locked = 0 rows, so a locked-heavy corpus read as 'found N, processed 0' with no reconciliation (mapped + unmapped < count). Pre-existing asymmetry made visible by the 2.5.2 mapped/unmapped exposure.
issues.fix_note: The fix-path issue dict now carries an additive `locked` counter (count - rows visible to the fixer) so mapped + unmapped + locked always reconciles with count. Regression: tests/test_source_normalization.py::test_fix_reports_locked_rows_it_cannot_touch.

issues.summary: do_store normalizes an explicit null source to {} at the write seam (v2.5.1 persisted the literal 'null', so recall returned source=None; 2.5.2 rows return {}), but the store tool description did not document the convergence — consumers could not know None and {} now denote the same anonymous producer, and legacy 'null' rows coexist with new '{}' rows in the same corpus.
issues.fix_note: Deliberate contract change (2.5.x charter: contract drift allowed when intentional and documented). The store tool's source description now states that null is normalized to {} at the write seam and both persist (and recall) as the anonymous {}. Health checks already treated null and {} identically, so no behavioural fix was needed.

issues.summary: The no-persist branch of do_store returned {ok, id:'no-persist', persisted:false} without the `embedded` key that 2.5.2 added to the success contract, while the tool description read as if embedded were always present — a consumer treating it as required would KeyError under pause_persistence.
issues.fix_note: The skipped response now carries embedded:false (nothing was persisted), and the store tool description documents the no-persist shape with an instruction to branch on `persisted`. Regression: tests/test_no_persist.py::test_store_skipped_under_pause.

issues.summary: checkup.py's --db help text advertised a phantom '~/.claude/cpersona.db' default the code never implemented, and an unconfigured run (no --db, no CPERSONA_DB_PATH) silently resolved a different relative data/cpersona.db without announcing it, so an unattended cron or systemd run could monitor or --fix-create the wrong database.
issues.pattern: cpersona checkup: neither --db nor CPERSONA_DB_PATH is set
issues.fix_note: Rewrote the --db help to state the real resolution order (--db, else CPERSONA_DB_PATH, else the relative data/cpersona.db from cpersona.config), removing the phantom default, and added a branch that prints the resolved absolute DB path to stderr when neither --db nor CPERSONA_DB_PATH is set. Resolution behaviour is unchanged; the notice only reports the already-resolved path. Regression: tests/test_252a2_i1.py.

issues.summary: checkup.py _run had no try/finally around close_db(), so an exception during the checks (e.g. a corrupt or foreign DB missing the memories table) skipped close_db(); the non-daemon aiosqlite worker thread stayed alive and blocked interpreter shutdown, hanging the monitoring CLI forever instead of exiting.
issues.fix_note: Wrapped the check body of _run in try/except/finally: the finally always awaits close_db(), the except prints a readable 'error: checkup failed: <Type>: <msg>' to stderr and returns exit code 2. A corrupt or foreign DB now exits nonzero within about a second instead of hanging. Regression: tests/test_252a2_i1.py::test_c9_foreign_db_exits_nonzero_instead_of_hanging.

issues.summary: check_invalid_source_type and check_anonymous_source evaluated json_extract over every row's source; a single malformed-JSON source raised OperationalError which the bare 'except Exception: return []' swallowed, so BOTH checks reported the entire agent clean and masked genuine invalid-type and anonymous-source findings.
issues.fix_note: Added a leading json_valid(source) guard to the COUNT and fix-path SELECT in both checks; SQLite short-circuits AND left-to-right so a malformed row is excluded before json_extract runs (the guard MUST lead, empirically verified on sqlite 3.53.1). Malformed rows stay check_invalid_json's responsibility while the checks keep working over the rest of the corpus. Regression: tests/test_252a2_i2.py.

issues.summary: A legacy msg_id collision permanently blocked creation of the UNIQUE idx_memories_dedup_msg_id with no remediation path: the migration created the index without first resolving colliders, and no health check detected or repaired the index once the memories table existed.
issues.fix_note: The v12 migration (database.py) now runs a non-destructive UPDATE that keeps the newest (MAX id) colliding row's msg_id and blanks older unlocked colliders (locked rows honoured, no row deleted) before creating the index. Added a fix-capable health check check_dedup_msg_id_index (critical, registered before schema_objects so one fix pass converges) that recreates the index after the same collision resolution. Regression: tests/test_252a2_i2.py.

issues.summary: do_store set embedded=true whenever the remote /index POST did not raise; httpx does not raise on 4xx or 5xx, so a silently-rejected push (e.g. HTTP 500) still reported embedded=true, contradicting the store tool's documented contract that embedded reflects a successful push.
issues.fix_note: do_store's remote-index branch now captures the POST response and calls resp.raise_for_status() before setting remote_embedded=true; a non-2xx is routed into the existing except (logged at the same debug level as a transport error) so embedded reports true only when the push actually succeeded. The SQL row still persists. Regression: tests/test_252a2_i3.py.

issues.summary: The episode-boundary recall penalty used an agent-wide MAX(created_at) boundary that ignored the recall's project_id and channel scope, so an unrelated bucket's most-recent episode could decay an in-scope current-session memory to the penalty floor; the penalty runs by default.
issues.fix_note: _get_episode_boundary_ts now accepts optional project_id and channel and builds its MAX(created_at) query via isolation_where (the same gamma read semantics as the bug-107 confidence-span scoping); _apply_recall_scoring threads the in-scope project_id and channel into the call. project_id=None and channel='' preserve the agent-wide boundary for corpus-wide callers (gate calibration). Regression: tests/test_252a2_i3.py.

issues.summary: do_delete_episode deleted the SQL row but never removed the episode vector from the remote index, leaving an orphaned ep vector under the owner namespace; the sibling do_delete_memory path already purged the remote vector (bug-023), so episode deletion was asymmetric.
issues.pattern: a removal failure must not fail the delete
issues.fix_note: do_delete_episode now mirrors do_delete_memory's bug-023 removal path: it resolves the episode's owner agent_id up front (so the namespace is correct even when agent_id is omitted) and, after a successful DELETE, POSTs the ep removal to {base}/remove when VECTOR_SEARCH_MODE is remote. The removal is wrapped in try/except and logged non-fatally so a remote fault never fails the delete. Regression: tests/test_252a2_i4.py.

issues.summary: do_set_recall_precision's failure rollback restored a pre-await snapshot of the agent's beta, so when calibration failed a concurrent successful writer for the same agent_id could be silently clobbered back to this call's stale prev_beta.
issues.fix_note: The failure rollback is now compare-and-restore: on calibration failure it undoes its own mutation only if this call's write is still the live value (clear path: key still absent; set path: current beta still equals the resolved_beta this call wrote), otherwise it leaves a concurrent same-agent writer's applied value untouched. The solo-failure and solo-clear behaviours (bug-096) are preserved. Regression: tests/test_252a2_i4.py.

issues.summary: CPERSONA_HTTP_PORT (the streamable-HTTP bind) and CPERSONA_EMBEDDING_TIMEOUT_SECS (main()) were read with a bare int(os.environ...), reintroducing the bug-133 startup-crash class outside config.py: a malformed value raised an uncaught ValueError that aborted startup before the server listened.
issues.fix_note: Added public parse_int and parse_float wrappers in config.py delegating to the existing bug-133 warn-and-fall-back-to-default helpers, and extracted the two bare int() reads in server.py into module-level _resolve_http_port and _resolve_embedding_timeout that route through config.parse_int. A malformed value now warns and falls back to the default (8402 / 30) instead of raising. Valid and unset behaviour is preserved. Regression: tests/test_252a2_i5.py.

issues.summary: The no-persist pause is a bare process-global flag, but the streamable-HTTP transport serves every connected session from one process, so one client's pause_persistence silently dropped writes for all other sessions; the tool descriptions and the no_persist module docstring falsely implied per-session scope (the per-process equals per-session claim only holds under stdio).
issues.fix_note: Transparency-only treatment (no per-session state added; pause is still accepted on HTTP). Added an additive scope=process key to the pause, resume and status response payloads in the CPersona handlers (the shared vendored no_persist is untouched so CScheduler's shape is unchanged), rewrote the three tool descriptions to state the pause is process-wide and silences writes for every connected session under HTTP, and corrected the no_persist module docstring's false per-session claim. Regression: tests/test_252a2_i5.py. 2.5.7 (stage 2) superseded this in the safe direction: the pause is now keyed per declared session_key, so `scope` answers session for a declared caller and process only for the shared keyless bucket it still describes honestly. The marker moved to cpersona/session.py::_scope, because the server-side comment it used to pin described a global that no longer exists. It is anchored on the function definition rather than on a rendering site: the field is rendered in four places, so a pattern matching those would still pass after the field was dropped from three of them — precise about what it pins rather than appearing to pin more than it does. Per-control coverage is carried by tests/test_257_session_key_stage2.py::test_scope_is_reported_on_all_three_controls, which asserts pause, resume and status each report it.

issues.summary: verify-issues.sh joined the 7 registry fields with a literal pipe and re-read them with a pipe IFS, so an issue whose pattern legitimately contained a pipe character (bug-012's trigger regex) shifted every following field and its check silently evaporated (140 verdict lines for 141 issues) while the gate still exited 0.
issues.fix_note: Switched the record separator to an ASCII unit separator (0x1f) in both the Python emitter and the bash reader (the separator cannot occur in the registry's human-authored JSON), added a defensive emitter assertion that aborts nonzero if any field contains the separator or a newline, and a post-loop transport reconciliation that fails the gate when the emitted record count differs from the parsed row count. bug-012 is now evaluated and no row can be silently dropped. Regression: tests/test_252a2_i6.py.

issues.summary: The documented vendor-sync procedure (a blind rsync -a --delete mirror from ../mgp-py) would silently revert the three cpersona-local vendored patches (bug-019, bug-103, bug-104), including MEDIUM bug-019, because those fixes were never pushed upstream.
issues.fix_note: Added a post-sync reconciliation gate to sync-vendored-mcp-common.sh that runs verify-issues.sh (hard gate over the fix markers) plus the two pinned regression tests, failing the sync nonzero on any red, and a CAUTION header stating the vendored copy carries patches not yet upstream. This is a redundancy and faster-local-signal layer: the correctness regression is already blocked from shipping by the CI gates. The root fix (pushing the three patches upstream to mgp-py) is a separate repo and out of scope. Demonstrated non-destructively because running the real rsync is destructive.

issues.summary: scripts/mutation-proof.py (the mutation-proof harness that pins the 2.5.2 refactor seams) was not wired into CI, so a behavioural regression that defeated a seam could merge without the mutation gate ever running.
issues.fix_note: Wired scripts/mutation-proof.py into CI as a new additive, blocking mutation-proof job pinned to Python 3.13 (uv sync --dev then uv run --frozen python scripts/mutation-proof.py, with a 15-minute hang ceiling). No separate behaviour-golden step was added because capture-behaviour.py --check is already gated by the existing pytest job via tests/test_equivalence_252.py. No existing job or step semantics were changed. Test-first is waived (workflow-config wiring, no product code to regression-test); verified by capturing exit 0 for both wired scripts.

issues.summary: (LOW) Write-path size caps were incomplete: do_update_memory bypassed the MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH cap do_store enforces (an edited row could grow past it and the uncapped string was sent verbatim to the embedding backend), and the JSON sidecars source / metadata plus the episode summary / keywords had no bound at all — one call could park an arbitrarily large blob per row with no health check to surface it.
issues.pattern: content has been capped since 2.1, its JSON sidecars never were
issues.fix_note: source / metadata are bounded by MAX_METADATA_LENGTH and an oversized field is REFUSED (result='rejected') rather than truncated, because a truncated JSON document is not a JSON document. The episode's prose fields follow the memory rule instead — capped via _sanitize_content in the shared _prepare_episode_row seam (so the queue drain is bounded by the same rule) with truncated:true reported, and the remote index receives the stored text rather than the caller's original. do_update_memory enforces the same content cap as do_store. Regression: tests/test_252b1_writepath.py + tests/test_252b1_audit.py. Audit id: C12.

issues.summary: (LOW) recall_with_context built its recall exclude-filter from EVERY external_context entry but merged only role=user / role=assistant entries into the response, so a system or tool entry could suppress a matching memory while being absent from the output — the memory vanished with nothing in the response explaining why.
issues.fix_note: The filtering is kept (the caller does hold that text, so excluding it is correct); the silence is not. When entries whose role is not merged into `messages` are present, the response carries context_filter_only={roles:[...]} and the tool description states the asymmetry. Regression: tests/test_252b1_writepath.py. Audit id: C13.

issues.summary: (LOW) The /index push on the store WRITE hot path passed no timeout and inherited the embedding client's 30s DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_SECS, while every sibling remote call states a short dedicated deadline (health probe 3s, remote search 5s since bug-033) — a hung endpoint therefore blocked each store for ~30s, leaving the write path less protected than the read path against the same failure.
issues.fix_note: CPERSONA_REMOTE_INDEX_TIMEOUT_SECS (default 10s) is stated explicitly on the POST. Longer than the 5s search deadline because indexing does the embedding work server-side and a failure here is non-fatal (embedded=false) rather than a retriever fallback. Regression: tests/test_252b1_writepath.py. Audit id: #361 item (6).

issues.summary: (LOW) Several registered tool descriptions had drifted from the behaviour an MCP client sees: check_health claimed a 20-check registry against 23 implemented checks, deep_check said fix=true applies repairs while four of its six checks ignore the flag, pause_persistence listed 8 of the 14 write tools it silences and omitted the check_health/deep_check fix-downgrade, the @auto project_id sentinel was documented only on store though six tools resolve it, recall's source_id omitted the channel-scoped episode exception, and store's success shape omitted truncated.
issues.fix_note: Counts and lists are RENDERED from the code they describe (HEALTH_CHECK_NAMES, checks.DEEP_FIX_CAPABLE, the shared @auto clause) rather than restated in prose, and three structural gates in tests/test_structural_gates.py (Gates 7-9) fail CI when the declared set, the pause list or the @auto documentation falls behind the implementation. Audit id: C26.

issues.summary: (LOW) Remote-mode vector recall re-hydrated every hit with its own awaited SELECT ... WHERE id = ?, so a limit=100 recall paid 100 sequential SQLite round trips on the read hot path (aiosqlite funnels every statement through one background thread). Measured: 102 execute_fetchall calls for 102 hits.
issues.pattern: ONE query per row type instead of
issues.fix_note: _fetch_rows_by_id issues one IN() statement per row type (ids bound, never interpolated, chunked at 500 to stay under SQLite's bound-variable ceiling that a large limit could otherwise breach). Remote score order is preserved by replaying a separate `ordered` list rather than trusting IN() row order, and a hit whose row is gone is still skipped silently (stale remote index entry, pinned by the sv-remote-stale-id golden scenario). Measured 102 round trips -> 2 for 102 hits. Regression: tests/test_252b1_audit.py. Audit id: C16.

issues.summary: (LOW) The tool surface answered failures in two shapes: 5 sites returned {ok:false, error} while 29 returned a bare {error} with no ok key, so a caller branching on `ok` — the field every other response carries — read None for most failures and could not distinguish a refused call from a successful one. Same defect class as the store response contract (bug-156/b1-1), spread across delete/update/lock/unlock_memory, delete_episode, delete_agent_data, export/import/merge_memories, get_contents, set_recall_precision and the pause_persistence validation path.
issues.fix_note: utils.error_response(message, **extra) is the single constructor for a tool-level failure: it always carries ok=False and error, and **extra keeps the per-tool fields a failure still owes its caller (archive_episode's episode_id, import's errors list). All 31 sites converted. Gate 11 in tests/test_structural_gates.py fails CI on any returned dict literal carrying 'error' without 'ok' (tuple returns scanned too), so the shape cannot fork again. Regression: tests/test_252b1_writepath.py. Audit id: C23. Qualified 2026-07-29 (bug-185): "All 31 sites converted" describes the HANDLER surface only. The outermost MCP dispatch — vendored, cross-consumer — still answers an unknown tool name and an escaped handler exception with a bare {error} and no ok, and successful read tools carry no ok either, so the shape has not been made universal and this note should not be read as claiming it was.

issues.summary: (H-01) _prepare_episode_row applies the empty-summary guard to the RAW value and only then sanitizes, so a summary that sanitizes to empty ('[Memory from x]', whitespace) clears the guard and archive_episode writes an episode row with an empty summary while answering ok:true. The same commit rejects that exact input in store (result:'rejected'), so the two write paths disagree; the empty text is also handed to the vector index and renders in recall as a bodiless '[Episode] '.
issues.note: New in this branch: on master the annotation-only summary was stored verbatim. Fix direction: sanitize first, then apply the guard, so the refusal sees the value that would actually be written. Regression must cover the sanitize-to-empty input on BOTH the direct call and the queue drain (they share this seam).
issues.fix_note: The emptiness guard now judges the sanitized text — what would actually be stored — in BOTH places it lives. do_archive_episode sanitizes before its bug-006 guard so a summary that sanitizes away is refused with the established {ok:false, episode_id:None, error} shape; _prepare_episode_row sanitizes before its own guard and keeps raising ValueError, because tasks.py's drain depends on that exception to route a summary-less payload to retry/discard (returning a dict there would make the drain treat it as a row). An isinstance check keeps a non-string summary on the same refusal path instead of letting _sanitize_content raise TypeError. The truncated signal still reads the raw length, so the C12 cap regression is unaffected. Regression: tests/test_252b1_writepath.py::test_summary_that_sanitizes_to_empty_is_refused (3 inputs), ::test_summary_that_survives_sanitization_still_stores (positive control), ::test_prepare_still_raises_for_the_queue_drain (drain contract). Verified by mutation: reverting the guard fails 3 of them.

issues.summary: (H-02) The C13 disclosure builds filter_only_roles with sorted({...}) over unvalidated e.get('role'), so an external_context carrying roles of mixed types (int and str) raises TypeError and takes down the whole recall_with_context call. The tool's JSON Schema constrains external_context only to items:{type:object}, so the client is never told the property must be a string.
issues.note: Same defect class as bug-035, which is recorded in this file's own _ctx_content docstring ~80 lines above: an ill-typed context entry turns the whole tool into an opaque error. Fix direction: coerce the role to str at the same seam _ctx_content already guards, and tighten the schema. The merge loop's e.get('role','') == 'assistant' comparison is type-safe; only the new sorted() breaks.
issues.fix_note: _ctx_role() joins _ctx_content() as the type-safe accessor for external_context entries: a non-string role is coerced with str() before it reaches the set or sorted(), which closes both halves of the fault (an unhashable dict/list role broke while the set was built, a mixed int/str set broke in sorted()). The malformed role is now disclosed as its string form rather than aborting the call. The merge path still admits only the literal 'user'/'assistant', so coercion cannot promote a malformed entry into messages. The tool schema now states role/content as strings (they were advertised in prose only). Regression: tests/test_252b1_writepath.py::test_mixed_type_roles_do_not_abort_the_recall, ::test_unhashable_role_does_not_abort_the_recall, ::test_a_non_string_role_is_never_read_as_conversational. Verified by mutation: reverting the coercion fails all three.

issues.summary: (H-03) Gate 11 walks PKG.glob('*.py') non-recursively, so it cannot see _vendored_mcp_common/, where the outermost MCP dispatch still answers an unknown tool name and every escaped exception with a bare {error: ...} carrying no ok key. bug-161's fix_note claims all 31 sites were converted and that the gate makes the shape unable to fork again; the last site that can fork is outside the gate's reach.
issues.note: The vendored tree is a cross-consumer surface (cpersona-version-line-charter section 6), so the fix here is NOT to edit mcp_utils.py: it is to state the exception where the claim is made (bug-161 fix_note, README, SKILL.md) and either extend the gate's scan or record why the vendored seam is out of scope. Escalating the shape upstream is a separate clotohub-servers common bump. Update 2026-07-25: the current (defective) shape is now PINNED by tests/test_mcp_dispatch.py::test_an_unknown_tool_answers_the_outermost_shape and ::test_an_escaped_exception_answers_the_outermost_shape (bug-177), so it can no longer drift silently and the upstream fix has a test to invert. Those assertions must be inverted, not deleted, when the vendored wrapper is corrected. Update 2026-07-29: the remaining half of this prescription — stating the exception in bug-161 fix_note, README and SKILL.md — landed as bug-185.
issues.fix_note: The investigation found the gate had TWO blind spots, and closing either alone catches nothing: the scan was non-recursive (PKG.glob) so the vendored tree was never opened, AND the rule only matched a dict RETURNED literally, so the actual offending shape — a dict serialised on the way out, `return [TextContent(text=json.dumps({...}))]` — stayed invisible even to a recursive scan. Measured: recursive-only catches 0, extended-rule-only catches 0, both together catch 5. The gate now walks PKG.rglob and also inspects dicts handed to json.dumps() inside a return. The five vendored sites (mcp_utils.py x2 = the bug-164 shape itself, llm_provider.py x3) are waived by EXACT INVENTORY rather than by narrowing the scan back down: a new violation in cpersona's own modules fails, and so does any change to the vendored counts — which is the correct outcome at re-vendor time, since it means the upstream shape moved. Editing the vendored tree here is still forbidden (cross-consumer, charter section 6); the behavioural pins live in tests/test_mcp_dispatch.py (bug-177) and must be inverted, not deleted, when upstream fixes the shape. Teeth: test_error_shape_gate_sees_a_serialised_body and test_error_shape_gate_reaches_the_vendored_tree.

issues.summary: (M-01) SKILL.md and README both state that every tool-level failure carries ok:false alongside error, but store's rejection path (_store_rejected) returns {ok:false, result:'rejected', reason:...} with no error key. A caller following the published contract reads resp['error'] on a rejected store and gets a KeyError. Only the operating-context refusal carries error.
issues.note: SKILL.md is installed onto user disks (Gate 10 treats it as a published contract), so this is a shipped-contract error rather than internal prose. Fix direction: either add error to _store_rejected (contract change, ladder applies) or narrow both claims to what the code does. README line 23 carries the same sentence.
issues.fix_note: The claim was narrowed to what the code does rather than adding `error` to _store_rejected: `ok: false` is what every tool-level failure carries and what a caller branches on; the explanation travels in `error` everywhere except store, which puts it in `reason` beside result:'rejected'. Unifying the shape instead would be a tool-contract change (ladder applies) and would leave two redundant explanation fields on store, so it is deliberately NOT done here. Both published copies updated: skills/cpersona-memory/SKILL.md (installed on user disks) and README.md's 2.5.2 pre-release paragraph.

issues.summary: (M-02) The pause_persistence description asserts that all 14 write tools return a no-op carrying `persisted: false` and `id: "no-persist"`. Measured against the paused handlers, id:'no-persist' appears in 2 of 14 (store, archive_episode); migrate_channel_axis carries neither key because it returns a dry-run/repairs_skipped body without going through make_skipped_response. A caller detecting a paused session by id therefore misreads delete_memory's pause response as an ordinary failure.
issues.note: Not a regression (the same overclaim predates this branch) but the C26 fix widened its scope from 8 tools to 14. Gate 8 only checks that each tool NAME appears in the prose and says so in its own comment, so completeness is gated while truth is not. Fix direction: describe persisted:false as the single detection axis and treat id:'no-persist' as store/archive-only, or make the no-op bodies uniform.
issues.fix_note: Rewritten from source rather than from the claim: make_skipped_response replaces `id` only when the success body HAS one (store, archive_episode), blanks the action-specific id keys to null, and always merges persisted:false + dry_run:true + reason. migrate_channel_axis never reaches that builder — maintenance_handlers forces effective_dry_run when paused — so it carries no persisted key and is now described separately. The description names `persisted: false` as the authoritative signal and demotes the id sentinel to a per-tool detail. migrate_channel_axis is still named in the prose, so Gate 8's completeness check still passes.

issues.summary: (M-03) README describes the health check as 'a 20-check registry'; len(HEALTH_CHECK_NAMES) is 23. The same branch rendered this number from the constant in the tool description (f-string over HEALTH_CHECK_NAMES) and removed it from SKILL.md, but left the literal in the README it was editing in the same commit.
issues.note: Fix direction: drop the count or gate it the way the tool description now is. Hand-maintained counts in the README have gone stale repeatedly (see also bug-174).
issues.fix_note: The count was dropped rather than corrected to 23. A hand-maintained number in the README has no gate behind it (Gate 12 covers only the test-function figure), so correcting it just resets the clock on the same drift; the tool description already renders the true number from len(HEALTH_CHECK_NAMES) for anyone who needs it.

issues.summary: (M-04) The store tool's JSON Schema contradicts itself: the content property description still says 'Empty content is skipped.' while the tool description 30 lines above declares that empty content is rejected (ok:false, result:'rejected'). Under the b1-1 vocabulary 'skipped' specifically means ok:true, so a client reading only the property description treats an empty store as a harmless no-op and never branches on the failure.
issues.note: Single-line fix inside the same schema object that b1-1 already rewrote.
issues.fix_note: The content property now says empty (or sanitizes-to-empty) content is refused with ok:false, result:'rejected', matching the tool description 30 lines above and the b1-1 vocabulary in which 'skipped' specifically means ok:true.

issues.summary: (L-01) do_archive_episode_boundary's operating-context refusal returns _oc_reject(error) without episode_id, while the handler's own refusal carries episode_id:None and utils.error_response documents that field as the canonical example of what a failure still owes its caller. A caller reading resp['episode_id'] hits a KeyError only on the operating-context path.
issues.note: Reaching it requires an operating-context sidecar plus an unknown project_id. tests/test_252b1_writepath.py pins only the handler-side path.
issues.fix_note: do_archive_episode_boundary's operating-context refusal now returns {**_oc_reject(error), 'episode_id': None}, matching every other archive_episode failure (the handler's own refusal, the or_queue wrapper's, the paused no-op) and the field utils.error_response names as the archetype of what a failure still owes its caller. The read-only boundaries (recall / recall_with_context / list_*) were checked for the same asymmetry and do not have it: their handlers do not carry the collection field on failure either, so _oc_reject alone is consistent there.

issues.summary: (L-02) The keywords half of the C12 episode write-path cap is untested: deleting `keywords = _sanitize_content(keywords)` leaves the full suite green (642 passed). The oversize branch of the same field (len(keywords) > MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH) is likewise unexercised; the C12 regression covers summary only.
issues.note: Mutation verified on a git-archive copy outside the working tree.
issues.fix_note: Two regressions cover the keywords half of the C12 episode cap — the truncation branch (len > MAX reports truncated:true and stores exactly MAX) and the sanitize branch (an annotation-only prefix is stripped). Both were the surviving mutations.

issues.summary: (L-03) The batched id hydration added for bug-158 has no test that crosses _ID_FETCH_CHUNK: restricting the chunk loop to its first chunk leaves the suite green (642 passed), and the largest hit count any test produces is 102 against a chunk size of 500. The SQLite bound-variable ceiling that motivated the batching is therefore never exercised.
issues.note: Mutation verified on a git-archive copy outside the working tree. A test seeding >500 hits, or a temporarily lowered chunk size, closes it.
issues.fix_note: The chunk size is monkeypatched down to 2 over 5 rows rather than seeding 500+ rows, so the multi-statement path runs in the same 0.2s the rest of the file takes. A second case pins duplicate-id collapse across the boundary. This kills the surviving mutation (restricting the loop to its first chunk).

issues.summary: (L-04) context_filter_only is attached whenever a non-user/assistant entry carries content, without checking that anything was actually suppressed, while the tool description states those entries 'suppressed matching memories'. The regression asserts the disclosure appears against an empty corpus, where suppression cannot have happened, so the over-reporting is pinned as intended behaviour.
issues.note: Fails safe (over-disclosure, not silence), so the wording may be the thing to fix rather than the logic.
issues.fix_note: The wording was corrected rather than the logic: the disclosure is an honest statement that entries of those roles filtered the recall without appearing in the output, which is what the code checks. Claiming they 'suppressed matching memories' asserted an outcome the handler never measures. Making the logic match the old prose would mean diffing the recall with and without the context filter — real cost on the hot path to sharpen a disclosure that already fails safe. Registry anchor note: the entry was filed against memory_handlers.py (where the disclosure is built) but the overclaim and its fix live in the tool description in server.py, so the anchor moved with the fix.

issues.summary: (L-05) Behaviour-suite scenario descriptions still use the pre-b1 vocabulary: store-empty-content and store-sanitized-empty describe themselves as "skipped" while the pinned golden result is result:'rejected', and four health-* scenarios describe a healthy=True/False verdict that the response no longer carries. The golden values themselves match the implementation; only the prose drifted.
issues.note: These strings are what a reader consults to learn what the golden pins, so stale prose here misdescribes the contract the suite is enforcing.
issues.fix_note: Six `covers` strings re-worded to the post-b1 vocabulary (two store scenarios: skipped -> rejected; four health scenarios: the retired healthy boolean removed, status kept). The golden stores `covers` verbatim and test_equivalence_252 compares strings exactly, so both sides were rewritten in one pass with a per-string occurrence assertion; the resulting golden diff is exactly 6 lines and touches no observed value.

issues.summary: (L-06) The README test-count badge reads tests-646 while the suite collects 647. Gate 12's regex only checks the '**N test functions**' figure, so the badge the branch's final commit set out to keep current is outside the gate and is already off by one.
issues.note: Either extend Gate 12 to the badge or stop printing an exact count in it.
issues.fix_note: The badge no longer prints a count (tests-passing), which removes the drift class instead of resetting it — the collected-case count cannot be gated by Gate 12's AST walk anyway, because parametrised cases are not test functions. The '**N test functions**' figure Gate 12 does cover was refreshed to the measured 556 / 655 cases.

issues.summary: (L-07) The truncated flag is computed from the raw length before annotation stripping (len(raw_content) > MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH), so content whose annotation prefix pushes the raw string over the cap is reported truncated:true even though the stored text was never cut. update_memory's description promises the flag marks an actual cap hit.
issues.note: Pre-existing in do_store; this branch copied the same expression into do_update_memory (admin_handlers.py). Compare the sanitized length instead.
issues.fix_note: The flag now comes back from the seam that does the cutting: sanitize_content_with_flag() returns (content, truncated) and _sanitize_content() delegates to it, so the answer cannot disagree with what was stored. All THREE copies of the old `len(raw_content) > MAX` expression were converted — do_store, do_update_memory (where this branch had just duplicated it), and the episode path in do_archive_episode, which computed the same thing from its own locals. Leaving any one behind would have re-seeded the drift. Regression: test_truncated_reports_a_cut_not_a_long_argument plus a positive control and an episode case.

issues.summary: (L-08) The content/metadata caps introduced as 'bound the write path' are applied in do_store, do_update_memory and _prepare_episode_row only; do_import_memories and do_merge_memories write memory rows with no cap at all. config.py's own comment motivates the cap by 'one call could park an arbitrarily large blob per memory', which import satisfies.
issues.note: Faithful restore may be the intended semantics for import, in which case the claim's scope is what needs narrowing. checks.py's oversized_content detects the result after the fact, so impact is bounded.
issues.fix_note: The claim's scope was narrowed rather than the caps extended. import_memories and merge_memories restore or move rows that were already accepted under some earlier cap, and silently truncating (or refusing) a user's own backup at restore time is worse than admitting an oversized row — so the boundary is AUTHORING seams bounded, replayed rows detected after the fact by check_health's oversized_content. The config comment now states that division instead of implying a cap that covers every write. SUPERSEDED IN PART (2.5.5, bug-221): the boundary is now drawn on provenance, not authoring — import_memories DOES sanitise (its file may come from another DB, an older version or a hand edit; refusals and truncations are counted per line in the tally errors), while the intra-DB merge stays verbatim. The original rationale is preserved above for the merge half only.

issues.summary: (M-05) No test in the suite goes through the MCP dispatch layer: registry._handlers has zero test references, so every response-shape assertion in the 2.5.2b1 contract work calls handlers directly and bypasses the wrapper that actually serializes tool results to a client. Whether the new failure shape survives the real transport is unverified by any gate in this repository.
issues.note: Structural sibling of bug-164: the shape is gated everywhere except where it leaves the process. Same class as previously observed defects where a schema was never advertised and the change was inert in production while direct-call tests stayed green. The fix lands in tests/, not in the vendored file.
issues.fix_note: tests/test_mcp_dispatch.py drives a real ClientSession against registry.server over the MCP SDK's in-memory transport (mcp.shared.memory.create_connected_server_and_client_session), so the assertions are about what a client parses after a JSON-RPC round-trip rather than what a handler returned. Five cases: a successful store; the b1-1 refusal contract (ok:false + result:'rejected' + reason) surviving the transport; the ADVERTISED schema matching what the handler reads (store's agent_id/message, and recall_with_context's external_context item type from bug-163) — the inert-in-production class, where a handler accepts an argument the tool never advertises; and the two outermost failure paths from bug-164, pinned as they are today. Verified by mutation: stripping the advertised role/content schema fails the schema case, and reshaping _store_rejected fails the refusal case (both reverted, files restored by hash). The fix is test-only — the dispatch wrapper itself lives in the vendored tree.

issues.summary: (L-09) The registry's own $schema points at qa/issue-registry.schema.md, which does not exist anywhere in the tree. Nothing dereferences it, so no gate notices; a contributor following the pointer to learn the entry format finds nothing.
issues.note: Found by the parent agent while reading the registry format, not part of the diff review. Either add the schema doc or point at the ClotoCore original this mirrors.
issues.fix_note: The schema doc the $schema key pointed at now exists. It documents the entry fields, how `expected` flips across a fix (open entries anchor the DEFECT, fixed entries anchor the FIX), and the two pattern-selection traps hit twice while closing this batch: a pattern that is not unique in its file can never go absent, and the `file` field must follow the anchor when a fix lands somewhere other than where the report filed it.

issues.summary: (L-10) The branch's own tests/test_structural_gates.py carried two ruff violations — an unused `from cpersona import checks as checks_module` in test_deep_fix_gate_has_teeth and an f-string with no placeholders in the Gate 11 failure message — so the CI lint job (uvx ruff@0.15.21 check .) was red on this branch while master linted clean. The 2.5.0b1 audit added lint as a gate precisely because drift accumulates invisibly when CI runs pytest only; the file that implements the new gates was itself the drift.
issues.fix_note: Dropped the unused import and the extraneous f prefix. Found by the parent agent while running the CI gates against the fixes for bug-162/163 — the code review that produced bug-162..bug-178 ran pytest, verify-issues and mutation-proof but not ruff, so a red gate sat under a report that read as green. Isolated against a master worktree copy before attributing it to the branch. Registry anchor note: the unused import cannot serve as the absent-pattern — two OTHER test functions in the same file import checks_module and use it — so the anchor is the f-string violation, which the fix removed and which occurs once.

issues.summary: Under CONFIDENCE_ENABLED (production), rows admitted only via the FTS / keyword channels in _recall_rrf / _recall_rsf reach _apply_recall_scoring with _cosine=None even when their embedding blob sits in the DB; _compute_confidence's None-branch (sqrt(time_decay) * ...) is >= its cosine-branch (sqrt(norm_cos*time_decay) * ...), so vector-less rows structurally out-score real vector hits and invert the fusion intent (the keyword channel is documented to help DOWN-rank lexical contaminants).
issues.fix_note: Added memory_handlers._backfill_cosines, invoked from _apply_recall_scoring after the empty-results early return and BEFORE the episode-boundary penalty (so the penalty scales backfilled cosines uniformly with native ones), gated on CONFIDENCE_ENABLED so confidence-off deployments stay byte-for-byte identical. For each row that reaches scoring with _cosine=None, a positive integer id, and is not a profile sentinel (id=-1), the fix re-embeds the query (cache hit against the vector-channel call), fetches the embedding blob from the correct table per row kind (bug-040/041: memories and episodes AUTOINCREMENT independently so their integer ids collide and an episode id N must not read memory id N's blob), filters ragged widths (bug-085 tolerance), and materialises the true cosine on r['_cosine'] so downstream confidence scoring, episode-penalty scaling and the b1-4 match_reason.cosine surface it naturally. The batched cosine math is shared with the local scanners via a new vector._cosine_batch helper so the two paths cannot silently drift. The raw_cosine=None branch of _compute_confidence is unchanged: rows with genuinely no/ragged blob keep today's elevated score (production count is zero), deferred to the 2.6.0 scoring redesign. Regression: tests/test_bug155_cosine_backfill.py + tests/behaviour_252.py::recall-cosine-backfill. Ledger hygiene 2026-07-29 (bug-197): fixed_in read "unreleased" while v2.5.2b2 was tagged and on PyPI — and this is the fix that release note leads with, so an operator grepping the ledger for the ranking inversion would conclude no upgrade existed.

issues.summary: (C15) Under VECTOR_SEARCH_MODE=remote with STORE_BLOB=false the local cosine scan — the documented safety net for a remote /search outage — is structurally empty for memories: do_store skips the local blob for every row, so the scan's `embedding IS NOT NULL` predicate matches nothing. A /search fault with a working /embed then returns zero vector hits while the degraded advisory stays silent (it observes the embed boundary only), so recall drops to FTS/keyword in exactly the configuration that has no fallback, with nothing saying so.
issues.note: Adjudicated 2026-07-25 as (a) fix in 2.5.2, additive only. Not reachable in the operating deployment: bin/systemd/ctools/cpersona.service sets neither CPERSONA_VECTOR_SEARCH_MODE nor CPERSONA_STORE_BLOB, so it runs local mode with blobs stored. Same family as bug-164 / bug-177 ('green but powerless') closed in 2.5.2b1. Implementing it surfaced bug-182, the sharper half of the same blind spot.
issues.fix_note: Disclosure, not a behaviour change: the new report-only check `vector_fallback_config` (info) states the trade on the maintenance surface, and the boot path logs it once when an embedding client is configured. The advisory contract was deliberately NOT widened to the /search boundary — health.py scopes itself to embed availability by design, and redefining that mid-soak would blur a behaviour change with a regression.
